repository:github:bartoszadamczyk/pico-i.rationale: The maintainer README describes this as a complete IR library for Raspberry Pi Pico and makes no broader host claim.

repository:github:micropython/micropytho.rationale: The aggregate manifest installs the L2CAP component, so it requires a Bluetooth build that exposes the L2CAP API; the selected board stubs include that surface.
The official LCD160CR driver uses the Pyboard X/Y bus identifiers; the selected PYBV11 stubs expose those board-specific identifiers.
The driver requires the STM32 stm module with STM32WL5 sub-GHz radio support and defaults its antenna configuration to the NUCLEO-WL55 board.
The shared USB device implementation requires machine.USBDevice; the selected board stubs expose that low-level API.

repository:github:peterhinch/micropython.rationale: The maintainer README calls the library portable between hosts and records tests on ESP32 variants, Raspberry Pi Pico, and Pyboard.

repository:github:raspberrypifoundation/.rationale: The Raspberry Pi Foundation README defines picozero as a library for Raspberry Pi Pico and says it is aligned with that board.
